prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding the homeland of a people in the Psalm 83 confederacy against Israel, or one it recalls (Midian, Sisera)
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding the homeland of a people in the confederacy against Israel in Psalm 83:6-11 (Edom, the Ishmaelites, Moab, the Hagarenes, Gebal, Ammon, Amalek, the Philistines, Tyre, Assur), or a people or place the psalm recalls from earlier victories (Midian, the brook Kison, En-dor)
prompts.note: Philistine Gaza is in Palestine; Philistine Ashdod, Ashkelon, Ekron and Gath are in Israel, so both count.
prompts.summary: Psalm 83, a psalm of Asaph, describes nations that took crafty counsel to cut Israel off: Edom, the Ishmaelites, Moab, the Hagarenes, Gebal, Ammon, Amalek, the Philistines and Tyre, helped by Assur. The psalmist asks the Lord to deal with them as with Midian and with Sisera and Jabin at the brook Kison (Ps 83).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Edom, Moab and Ammon are in the confederacy (Ps 83:6-7).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Amalek is in the confederacy (Ps 83:7); the Bible Dictionary places Amalek in the desert of Paran, the central Sinai.

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Assur also is joined with them (Ps 83:8).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Philistine Ashdod, Ashkelon, Ekron and Gath lie in Israel (Ps 83:7); Sisera fell at the brook Kison (Ps 83:9).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: The inhabitants of Tyre join the confederacy (Ps 83:7).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: The Philistines are in the confederacy; their city Gaza is in the Gaza Strip (Ps 83:7).

answers.name: Saudi Arabia
answers.fact: The psalm recalls the Midianites (Ps 83:9); Church Bible Map 9 plots Midian east of the Gulf of Aqaba.

prompts.display_text: Pin an African country where the Church has between 5,000 and 20,000 members (end of 2025).
prompts.text_original: An African country where the Church had between 5,000 and 20,000 members at the end of 2025 (latest figures as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: Church facts and statistics country pages (31 Dec 2025)
prompts.summary: Nine African countries had between 5,000 and 20,000 members at the end of 2025: Cabo Verde (16,334), the Republic of the Congo (15,482), Angola (8,779), Togo (8,349), Benin (8,286), Malawi (7,857), Zambia (7,823), Tanzania (6,259) and Botswana (5,465). Cameroon (3,673) and Rwanda (3,625) were still under 4,000; Ethiopia has no published count.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory whose Church chronology records a revised or new Book of Mormon translation in its language.
prompts.text_original: Translations age, and the Church has issued new or revised Book of Mormon translations in several languages. Pin a country or territory whose Church chronology records a revised or new translation of the Book of Mormon in its language.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies: New Zealand, Russia, Hong Kong, Italy, Switzerland, Sweden, South Korea, Ukraine, Guatemala
prompts.summary: Translations get revised. The Maori Book of Mormon was reworked in 1917-19, Italian in 1951-65 by the Swiss Mission, Spanish in 1994, Korean in 2005, Chinese in 2007-08, Swedish in 2008 and Russian in 2012. Each revision aimed at clearer, more current language for members.

answers.name: Russia
answers.fact: A new Russian translation of the Book of Mormon was published in 2012.

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: The Swiss Mission translated and published new Italian editions in 1951-65.

answers.name: South Korea
answers.fact: New Korean translations of all three books were released in 2005.

answers.name: New Zealand
answers.fact: Matthew Cowley, Stuart Meha and William Duncan Sr. revised the Maori translation in 1917-19.

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: The Swiss Mission produced the new Italian editions of 1951-65.

answers.name: Guatemala
answers.fact: A new Spanish translation of the triple combination was released in February 1994.

answers.name: Sweden
answers.fact: New Swedish editions of the Book of Mormon and other scriptures came out in 2008.

answers.name: Ukraine
answers.fact: A revised Ukrainian Book of Mormon appeared in 2005.

answers.name: Hong Kong
answers.fact: A revised Chinese translation in traditional and simplified characters was published in 2007-08.

prompts.display_text: Pin a permanent member of the UN Security Council with a temple dedicated, under construction or announced (as of October 2026).
prompts.text_original: A permanent member of the United Nations Security Council with a temple dedicated, under construction or announced (as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronology; UN Security Council membership
prompts.summary: All five permanent members of the UN Security Council have a temple at some stage as of October 2026. The United States, the United Kingdom and France have dedicated temples, China has the Hong Kong temple with Shanghai announced, and Russia has an announced temple with no city named.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: More than 100 dedicated temples, from St. George (1877) on.

answers.name: France
answers.fact: Paris France Temple (2017).

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: London (1958) and Preston (1998) temples; Birmingham under construction.

answers.name: China
answers.fact: Hong Kong China Temple (1996); Shanghai temple announced in 2020.

answers.name: Russia
answers.fact: A temple in Russia was announced in 2018; no site named yet.

prompts.display_text: Pin an African country where the Church has 5 or more stakes as of October 2026.
prompts.text_original: An African country where the Church has 5 or more stakes (as of October 2026, year-end 2025 figures).
prompts.citation: Church facts and statistics country pages (figures of 31 Dec 2025) and Global Histories overviews, read 4 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: Eleven African countries have 5 or more stakes. Nigeria leads with 80, followed by the Democratic Republic of the Congo (44), Ghana (31), Ivory Coast (23) and South Africa (18). Smaller but fast-growing stake networks exist in Zimbabwe, Sierra Leone, Mozambique, Liberia, Madagascar and the Republic of the Congo.
